Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The same Blood Wave loop as the PTR meta build, re-geared for the one thing 3.2.0 actually gives the class. The Necromancer core-stat scalar rises from 1.25 to 1.625 - a 30% baseline damage buff per 10 Intelligence - and that is a bigger change to how the character should be geared than it looks, because the Season 14 gear model behind this build was built when Intelligence was worth 30% less and Essence Regeneration therefore won most contested affix slots. This variant moves Intelligence up the priority order wherever it competes with a quality-of-life stat rather than with the resource floor itself. It also takes the two other 3.2.0 facts seriously: Azurath is cut to single-target only, so nothing here treats it as a clear tool, and the patch offers no answer to the class's survivability, mobility or build-depth problems, so the defensive package stays intact rather than being traded for damage. Both aggregator class lists still put Necromancer at the bottom - D on one, C on the other - and a scalar buff does not move that, which the digest says in as many words: a baseline additive buff does not offset a gutted multiplier.

Rotation
  1. Move with Sever and Blood Mist, hold Blood Wave down, Blood Lance to dump Overpower and Bone Prison on survivors, while the curse loop runs itself in the background.
  2. Open on a small pull and build Resolve before you engage anything large.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Unchanged from the base build: Sever onto a pack for a corpse, Blood Mist to eat it and teleport, Blood Lance to dump Overpower, Blood Wave held to regain it, Bone Prison on survivors.
Move on when Kessime's Legacy equipped.

Early Endgame — [ptr] The curse loop runs itself: the Wat rune applies Decrepify, Life Tap makes Blood Orbs, the Teb rune spends them on Iron Maiden. Move with Sever and Blood Mist, hold Blood Wave.
Move on when Ring of Starless Skies online, at which point the base guide drops the Resource Cost Reduction requirement to over 15%.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Identical to the early endgame; the gear changes, not the gameplay.
Move on when Ready to rebuild around block chance and Resolve for the push stage - a different gear set, not a different rotation.

Pushing — [ptr] Open on a small pull and cast Blood Wave until Resolve is around 10 before engaging anything large - the base guide is blunt that engaging big packs from zero Resolve is an instant death. Then Blood Lance before every pack, Bone Prison before contact, Corpse Tendrils for Vulnerable and Flesh Eater, Blood Mist every eight seconds, Blood Wave held down.

Lootfilter

Blood Wave Necromancer - Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

[ptr] No Season 15 filter exists anywhere - InfinityBuilds' 57-filter directory is entirely Season 14 or earlier, checked 2026-08-09 - so this is the Season 14 build's own in-guide import code used as a floor. It still fits: the affix pool is unchanged on the PTR. One PTR-specific check before importing: make sure it is not hiding jewelry, because Soul Splinters socket into jewelry and the Splinter decision is a real one on this patch.

Uniques
  • pants [ptr] PTR route: Mrak, the PTR vendor beside the main Waypoint in any major city, hands out random uniques as part of his boosts - minutes rather than a farm. Live route, unchanged by 3.2.0: gamble pants at the vendor and target-farm Andariel (Hanged Man's Hall east of Tarsarak, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key). The build does not work without it. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool, so any lair boss, or a Horadric Cube conversion - and note that 3.2.0 reworks Mythic crafting into three routes, one of which lets the Jeweler pick the slot. Where →
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Mythic Unique from any lair boss, or crafted. 3.2.0's Mythic rework matters here - the Jeweler rune route and the Blacksmith cache both bypass the one-Crafted-Mythic cap, so a character can hold more Mythics on this patch than on live. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool or Horadric Cube. Listed for completeness because the base build uses it at the push stage; this variant deliberately does not - see the tweaks. Where →

How to run them

[ptr] Carried over from Season 14 unchanged, and that is a sourced statement rather than an assumption: the words 'Mercenary' and 'Mercenaries' and all four mercenary names are absent from the official 3.2.0 notes entirely, so the Season 14 system and pairings are the only guidance that exists. The guide publishes two pairings and switches between them. While you are still gearing it hires Aldkin, purely for the 15% Critical Strike Chance and the early sustain - 'getting critical strike chance to 100% is not as easy especially during the early game'. From the midgame on it hires Subo instead, for map visibility and a 25% Critical Damage multiplier, which is what the recorded tree above is. The Reinforcement never changes: Raheir on Bastion, 'great for survivability'. Icy Veins dissents and hires Varyana; Maxroll is the construction source here and its own author swaps mercenaries with progression, so the honest reading is that the hire is a tuning knob and Raheir/Bastion is the fixed part.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] The same Blood Wave loop as the PTR meta build, re-geared for the one thing 3.2.0 actually gives the class. The Necromancer core-stat scalar rises from 1.25 to 1.625 - a 30% baseline damage buff per 10 Intelligence - and that is a bigger change to how the character should be geared than it looks, because the Season 14 gear model behind this build was built when Intelligence was worth 30% less and Essence Regeneration therefore won most contested affix slots. This variant moves Intelligence up the priority order wherever it competes with a quality-of-life stat rather than with the resource floor itself. It also takes the two other 3.2.0 facts seriously: Azurath is cut to single-target only, so nothing here treats it as a clear tool, and the patch offers no answer to the class's survivability, mobility or build-depth problems, so the defensive package stays intact rather than being traded for damage. Both aggregator class lists still put Necromancer at the bottom - D on one, C on the other - and a scalar buff does not move that, which the digest says in as many words: a baseline additive buff does not offset a gutted multiplier.

Rotation
  1. Move with Sever and Blood Mist, hold Blood Wave down, Blood Lance to dump Overpower and Bone Prison on survivors, while the curse loop runs itself in the background.
  2. Open on a small pull and build Resolve before you engage anything large.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Unchanged from the base build: Sever onto a pack for a corpse, Blood Mist to eat it and teleport, Blood Lance to dump Overpower, Blood Wave held to regain it, Bone Prison on survivors.
Move on when Kessime's Legacy equipped.

Early Endgame — [ptr] The curse loop runs itself: the Wat rune applies Decrepify, Life Tap makes Blood Orbs, the Teb rune spends them on Iron Maiden. Move with Sever and Blood Mist, hold Blood Wave.
Move on when Ring of Starless Skies online, at which point the base guide drops the Resource Cost Reduction requirement to over 15%.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Identical to the early endgame; the gear changes, not the gameplay.
Move on when Ready to rebuild around block chance and Resolve for the push stage - a different gear set, not a different rotation.

Pushing — [ptr] Open on a small pull and cast Blood Wave until Resolve is around 10 before engaging anything large - the base guide is blunt that engaging big packs from zero Resolve is an instant death. Then Blood Lance before every pack, Bone Prison before contact, Corpse Tendrils for Vulnerable and Flesh Eater, Blood Mist every eight seconds, Blood Wave held down.

Uniques
  • pants [ptr] PTR route: Mrak, the PTR vendor beside the main Waypoint in any major city, hands out random uniques as part of his boosts - minutes rather than a farm. Live route, unchanged by 3.2.0: gamble pants at the vendor and target-farm Andariel (Hanged Man's Hall east of Tarsarak, Kehjistan; 1x Greater Lair Key). The build does not work without it. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool, so any lair boss, or a Horadric Cube conversion - and note that 3.2.0 reworks Mythic crafting into three routes, one of which lets the Jeweler pick the slot. Where →
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Mythic Unique from any lair boss, or crafted. 3.2.0's Mythic rework matters here - the Jeweler rune route and the Blacksmith cache both bypass the one-Crafted-Mythic cap, so a character can hold more Mythics on this patch than on live. Where →
  • amulet [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: General Unique Pool or Horadric Cube. Listed for completeness because the base build uses it at the push stage; this variant deliberately does not - see the tweaks. Where →

Reasoning

Based onBlood Wave Necromancer
Tweaks vs. the base build
  1. [ptr] Intelligence rises in the helm, weapon and ring priorities where it previously sat third. The 3.2.0 core-stat scalar takes Necromancer from 1.25 to 1.625 damage per 10 Intelligence, so every point is worth 30% more than the Season 14 gear model assumed.
  2. [ptr] The resource floor is not traded away for that. Blood Wave as a Core skill is still 'very resource hungry' in the base guide's words and 3.2.0 does not touch its cost, so Essence Regeneration and Resource Cost Reduction still lead the jewelry priorities - Intelligence gains only where the competing affix was a comfort stat.
  3. [ptr] Nothing on this page treats Azurath as a clear tool. 3.2.0 reduces it to single-target only. It is not named in any gear row here because the pinned 3.1.0 game database does not carry it at all, which is worth saying out loud rather than leaving as a silent omission.
  4. [ptr] The push stage keeps Banished Lord's Talisman instead of swapping to Blood-Mad Idol. The base build accepts that trade because the damage gain is large; 3.2.0 gives Necromancer no new survivability and both aggregator lists still rank the class last, so spending the class's weakest stat to buy its already-adequate one reads worse on the PTR than it did on live.
  5. [ptr] Soul Splinter guidance, which the base build predates: the obvious pick for a build gating on over 70% Critical Strike Chance is Splinter of Anguish, and it is the wrong one here - its cost is +30% Primary Resource costs on a build whose published failure mode is running out of Essence. Splinter of Pain (Damage Reduction for -30% Movement Speed) is the safer fit, and taking no Splinter at all is defensible until the resource maths has been re-measured on 3.2.0.
  6. [ptr] No War Plans are recorded, on either page. 3.2.0 changes nothing about the system, no per-build picks exist for any season, and the PTR vendor hands testers a maxed system anyway.

Generate Essence: 15

Blood Wave

UltimateBlood

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 50 seconds

Lucky Hit Chance: 50%

Conjure a tidal wave of blood that deals 500% damage and Knocks Back enemies.

Modifiers

  • OverpowerCasting Blood Wave overfills your Overpower by 2.
  • HematolagniaBlood Wave becomes a Core Skill, has no Cooldown, but costs 50 Essence. Blood Wave conjures a shorter wave that deals 300% damage and no longer Knocks Back enemies.

Blood Lance

CoreBlood

Rank 14/15

Essence Cost: 15

Lucky Hit Chance: 50%

Throw a blood lance, dealing 130% to an enemy that ricochets to another enemy. Enemies hit are lanced for 3 seconds.

When Blood Lance hits an enemy, it deals damage to all other lanced enemies.

Modifiers

  • OverpowerBlood Lance consumes 2 stacks of Overpower to throw an additional lance, dealing 50% of normal damage.
  • FortifyBlood Lance Fortifies you for 4% of your Maximum Life ({x}) if it hits an enemy already lanced.
  • Festering WoundBlood Lance becomes a Darkness Skill and deals Shadow damage. Enemies hit are permanently lanced and the lance deals 80% Corrupting damage per second to them.
Physical Damage

CoreShadow

Rank 1/15

Essence Cost: 20

Lucky Hit Chance: 40%

MacabreBone

Rank 15/15

Cooldown: 15 seconds

Unearth a prison of bone with {x} Life that surrounds the target area for 6 seconds.

  • Essence GenerationCasting Bone Prison generates 50 Essence. Trapping a Boss generates an additional 25 Essence.
  • Life ImprisonmentBone Prison becomes a Blood Skill, casting the prison around you. While standing within it your Essence Generation and Cast Speed are increased by 20%, but it drains 5% of your Maximum Life every second.
  • VulnerableBone Prison makes enemies Vulnerable for 8 seconds.

Rank 1/15

Cooldown: 24 seconds

Disperse into a bloody mist, becoming Immune for 3 seconds. You deal 420% damage to enemies and Heal for 6.0% of your Maximum Life ({x}) over the duration.

Thrillseeker

PassiveSubo

Your active Cooldowns are reduced by 0.5 seconds when an Explosive Charge explodes.

Explosive Charges now detonate after only 1.5 seconds.

Bargaining Chips

PassiveSubo

Targets stuck with Explosive Charges take 5%[x] increased damage per Explosive Charge stuck.

Incendiary Bolt

PassiveSubo

If Subo's Snipe hits the target he originally aimed at, a Molotov explodes on them.

Ambusher

PassiveSubo

You gain 20%[x] Lucky Hit Chance against enemies damaged by Subo's Salvo within the last 3 seconds.

Share a Drink

PassiveSubo

When one of Subo's Molotovs explodes, it has a 50% chance to drop a Healing Potion for you.

Scorched Earth

PassiveSubo

Subo's initial Molotov explosions cause enemies to take 30%[x] increased Damage Over Time from you for 3 seconds.

Mastermind

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Trap and Trip Mines explosions gain 60% Size.

You and Subo gain 25%[+] Crowd Control Duration.

Loaded Munitions

PassiveSubo

Subo's Wire Traps and Trip Mines inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 5 seconds.

Opening Fire

PassiveSubo

You deal 25%[x] increased Critical Strike Damage to enemies hit by Subo's Cover Fire for 4 seconds.

Pin Cushion

PassiveSubo

Subo's Cover Fire also Immobilizes enemies for 3 seconds.

Ready At Hand

PassiveSubo

Direct damage to an Elite grants you 20%[+] Movement Speed for 2 seconds.

Piercing Arrows

PassiveSubo

Subo's Heavy Shot now pierces through enemies.

Trip Mines

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 18 seconds

Subo scatters 3 explosive traps that each arm after 1.0 seconds. When an enemy moves within range of one, it explodes for 300% Physical damage and Knocks Down enemies for 1.5 seconds.

Cover Fire

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a countless volley of arrows, then unleashes it over your position for 140% Physical damage that Slows enemies by 50% for 4 seconds.

Explosive Charge

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Subo fires 4 Explosive Charges that stick to enemies. Each explodes after 6.5 seconds or when their target dies, dealing 60% Physical damage.

Snipe

Iconic skillSubo

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Subo charges a massive piercing bolt, then unleashes it forwards for 450% Physical damage that Knocks Back enemies.

Wire Trap

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 10 seconds

Weapon: Bow

Basic Attack: Heavy Shot

Subo places a concussive trap that arms after 0.8 seconds. When an enemy moves within range, it explodes for 80% Physical damage and Stuns enemies for 2.0 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo fires a toughened arrow at an enemy, dealing 80% Physical damage with a 30% chance to Stun for 1.0 seconds.

Molotov

Core skillSubo

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Crossbow

Basic Attack: Salvo

Subo tosses an incendiary at an enemy, dealing 10% Physical damage and Stunning them for 1.0 seconds before exploding into flames. For the next 5 seconds, enemies within the area repeatedly take 36% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Subo launches 5 bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Physical damage. The final bolt explodes, Slowing enemies by 50% for 2 seconds.
